_metric_engine_notes.revenue_estimate: NOT applicable — this installation compares embodied carbon, labour, time, and cost. Revenue and profit are not LCA metrics. No dataset exists for this in the project scope. Metric engine must return null for these fields.
_metric_engine_notes.profit_estimate: NOT applicable — same reason as revenue_estimate. Return null.
_metric_engine_notes.shape_factor_usage: Multiply all per-m2 values by the shape_factor from shape_factor_table before scaling by area_m2 × floors. Default = 1.0 (rectangle). This corrects for perimeter-to-area ratio — complex plan shapes have more wall area per unit of GFA.

shape_factor_table._note: Applied by the metric engine as: output = per_m2_value × shape_factor × area_m2 × floors. Based on perimeter-to-area ratio conventions in EN ISO 13789.

methods.name: MASONRY
methods.description: Load-bearing fired-clay brick, hand-laid on site. Catalan tier-1 data: Hispalyt EPDs, BEDEC (ITeC), CYPE. CO2: 205–490 kgCO2e/m2 GFA. Labour: 22–34 h/m2.
methods.source_label: Hispalyt GlobalEPD 008-016/017/001 + BEDEC ITeC + CYPE FEF010/FFZ010 (Tier 1, Catalonia)

confidence_range.note: Dominant Tier-1 Catalan EPDs — data measured in Catalonia, no geographic extrapolation needed.

methods.name: 3D PRINTED
methods.description: Robotic concrete extrusion. Structural walls only — foundation, roof, and openings use conventional construction. No published LCA for any Catalan project. Data from Qatar, Australia, and the US. CO2: 58–147 kgCO2e/m2 GFA.
methods.source_label: Mohammad 2020 (Qatar, T1) + Rossi 2024 (whole-house, T1) + Allouzi 2020 (Jordan, T1) — NO Catalan peer-reviewed LCA

confidence_range.note: Tier-1 sources but all from Qatar/Australia/Jordan — geographic extrapolation to Catalonia is required. No peer-reviewed 3DP LCA exists for Spain.

methods.name: PREFAB
methods.description: Factory-built modules (concrete) or cross-laminated timber (CLT) panels, assembled on site. No Spanish primary LCA. CLT sourced from Austria/Sweden: 1,800–2,200 km transport adds 25–60 kgCO2e/m2 not included in most studies. CO2: 130–350 kgCO2e/m2 GFA (range spans biogenic accounting methods).
methods.co2_note: Range spans CLT-with-biogenic-credit (130-220) to CLT-without-biogenic (220-350). Modular concrete is 280-569. The biogenic-carbon accounting choice alone swings the number by 30%.
methods.source_label: Andersen 2022 (CLT, T1) + Wei 2024 (modular concrete HK, T1) + Stora Enso EPD (Austrian CLT, T1) — NO Spanish/Catalan primary LCA
methods.geographic_tier: EU (no Spanish primary data; CLT = Austrian/Swedish)

confidence_range.note: Tier-1 EU sources but no Spanish/Catalan primary LCA. Biogenic carbon accounting choice alone swings the CO2 number by 30%. CLT transport Austria→Barcelona adds unmodelled uncertainty.

methods.name: RECLAIMED BRICK
methods.description: Salvaged fired-clay brick, cleaned and relaid. Comparison baseline: other methods are plotted against this. CO2 under cut-off method: 8–25 kgCO2e/m2 GFA (structure only). Same wall under system-expansion: 35–70 kgCO2e/m2. No Catalan tier-1 LCA; EU proxy data (Finland, Switzerland, UK). Labour: 2–4x higher than new brick.
methods.co2_note: Structure only (wall). Foundation and roof are conventional. The allocation rule choice drives a 5x swing — this must be surfaced in the projection wobble overlay.
methods.labor_hours_range: 2.5-6.5 h/m2 wall (2-4x more than new brick)
methods.source_label: RBC EPD 2024 (UK, T1) + Salmio & Huuhka 2026 (Finland, T1) + De Wolf 2020 (T1) + Devenes 2022 (Switzerland, T1) — NO Catalan tier-1 LCA
methods.geographic_tier: EU proxy (Finnish/Swiss/UK sources; no Catalan data; BEDEC has no reclaimed-brick entry)

confidence_range.note: Tier-1 EU sources but allocation rule (cut-off vs system-expansion) drives a 5x CO2 swing. No Catalan data. Used as baseline floor, not as a competitor — confidence applies to the range spread, not the method rank.

methods.role: BASELINE — not a 4th competitor. Other methods are plotted against this floor.

phases.name: FOUNDATION
phases.description: Structural base. Reinforced concrete strip or slab. Load transfer to ground. Consistent across all methods.

phases.name: STRUCTURE
phases.description: Load-bearing envelope. Method-specific layer. Primary contributor to embodied carbon.

phases.name: ROOF
phases.description: Weatherproofing layer. Pitched or flat. Conventional across all methods except where noted.

phases.name: OPENINGS
phases.description: Windows and doors. Aluminium, PVC, or timber frames. Not method-specific.

phases.name: FINISHING
phases.description: Interior and exterior surfaces. Render, plaster, paint, tile. Low embodied carbon; high labour intensity.

comparison_insight:
Embodied carbon, labour hours, construction time, and cost — side by side, per method. The numbers come from different places: Catalan kilns and BEDEC for masonry, research from Qatar and Australia for 3D printing, Austrian mill EPDs for CLT, Swiss and Finnish studies for reclaimed brick. Each figure carries a confidence level that reflects where it was measured and how far it travels.

Reclaimed brick sits below all three as the baseline. That number shifts by a factor of five depending on which accounting rule is applied — cut-off, avoided-burden, or system-expansion. That is not an error. It is a methodological choice, and every published LCA makes one.

The comparison does not tell you which method to choose. It shows what each choice costs, how well we can measure it here, and where the data runs out.
